Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

lines: # Game Design Document (working draft)
> Epic AI MegaJam 2026 · Theme: **DIRECTOR'S CUT** · Unreal Engine 5.9.0
-> Status: **v0.15, 2026-11-12** — owner's vision plus eleven rounds of answers. Anything marked **TBD** is not decided yet; see "Open questions" at the end.
+> Status: **v0.16, 2026-11-12** — owner's vision plus eleven rounds of answers. Anything marked **TBD** is not decided yet; see "Open questions" at the end.

> Audience: **the architect** = whichever Claude Code chat is currently implementing the game. There is normally only one at a time, and it is replaced when its context fills up or its tasks are done. This document is the source of truth that every new architect chat reads first. Implementation is delegated as `CLAUDE.md` says ("Implementador").
> Project code name: **Glyphbound** (provisional; the game title is still TBD). Written in English because it is part of the public dev log (Glass Box) and the jam requires English.
## Changelog
+- v0.16 (2026-11-12): owner asked for a way to reset the perks from the skill tree screen, to test them better. All spent skill points come back.

- v0.15 (2026-11-12): owner's second round of play-test notes. Jumps commit to their direction (no steering in the air; the second jump can pick a new direction and then commits too); the sword hits where the player aims, not the center of the target; sword hits and the staff's basic attack get the head / weak point bonus.

- v0.14 (2026-11-12): owner's first play-test. - defeating each **boss**;

content.content:
76	- **Second review (Codex, Sol 6.1 Medium, read-only): 4 findings, all real, all fixed by Muse Spark.** (1) An enemy's line-of-sight check treated "I hit another orc" as "I can see the player", even with a wall behind that orc. (2) The new steering fallback checked for obstacles but not for ground, so an enemy could steer itself off a platform. (3) The new Weapons page showed the element of the weapon type, not of the weapon the player forged. (4) Two visuals ignored values the data file defines. The reviewer also listed what it checked and found solid (stored ammo and elements, shield expiry, the single respawn on the death screen, damage-number cleanup, the material in the cook).
77	- **Where the AI failed in this block:** the smoke script's new shield screenshot was requested on the same frame the shield starts to rise, so the picture showed a "BLOCKING" label and no shield. Not a game bug, but a picture that would have misled a reader. Caught by the architect looking at the screenshot; the step is now split. Also still true: **none of this block has been played by a person yet** (mouse clicks while paused and the gamepad Block are only code-read).
78	
79	## Third block: the owner plays the second build
80	The owner played the second build and sent three more notes, then a correction while the work was running. One serial batch, so it went to Muse Spark alone (no parallel agents, no second review: about 300 lines, two new pure functions with tests).
81	
82	| Owner's note (translated) | What was done |
83	|---|---|
84	| "When jumping, the direction should not be changeable in the air; the second jump can choose where it goes, but then it cannot be changed. Like a jump in real life." | Air control is 0. The direction is chosen at takeoff from the movement keys held; the air jump picks a new one and commits again. The rule is one pure function, tested. The dash is untouched. |
85	| "The sword attack should decide where it hits, not always the center of the target." | The sword hits the point of the enemy's body closest to where the player aims (pure function, tested): look at the head, hit the head. |
86	| "Sword and staff (primary click) damage should get the bonus for hitting the head and / or weak point." | Before, the gun applied its own head bonus, the projectile only set a flag and the sword did nothing. Now there is ONE rule (`ApplyWeakPointBonus`) used by gun, staff and sword; it is the single place to extend when enemies get other weak points. |
87	| "Remember the rifle exists, also x1.5. The bonus must be raisable with perks." | Rifle 2 -> 1.5 in `Weapons.json`. No code needed for the perk: the existing weapon-tree node adds to `Weapon.All.HeadshotMult`, and since staff and sword now read that stat through the same lookup as guns, the perk already covers them. Its description was updated. |
88	
89	The last row is the modifier system doing its job: a design request that arrived mid-task cost one number and one sentence of text.
90	
91	## Design decisions
92	All taken by the architect; the owner asked not to be consulted on engineering. The provisional gameplay rules and numbers that had to be invented are listed in GDD section 18 for the owner to confirm or change.
93	
94	- **C++ only, built from the blank template.** The first-person template was not used: the jam asks for gameplay beyond Epic's templates, and AI agents handle C++ text far better than Blueprint graphs.
95	- **No Gameplay Ability System.** Considered (the GDD lists it as a candidate) and rejected: heavy boilerplate and asset setup for a 4-day jam. Replaced by three small pieces we fully control: one stat system (base value from data + stacked modifiers), one damage function, one status-effect component. Skill-tree nodes, armor, slows, potions, air passives and the weapon enchant are all "a named group of modifiers".
96	- **All gameplay numbers in JSON under `Content/Data`, shipped as loose files.** Git only carries text in this team, AI agents edit text reliably, and the owner can retune a packaged build with a text editor. `gb.ReloadData` reloads while playing.
97	- **Spells = data + a behavior class.** Each parameter has `Base / Min / Max / ScaledBy` (none, QTE power, QTE reach). Eight behaviors cover the nine active spells and the enchant; a new spell that fits a behavior is one JSON entry.
98	- **No binary assets needed to run.** The test arena, input actions and placeholders are built in C++; placeholder pixel art is rows of text turned into textures at runtime. The whole game is reviewable as text in git.
99	- **HUD drawn with the canvas, not widgets.** The two skins (90s RPG with the staff, cyberpunk with a gun) are two style structs.
100	- **Death keeps what was collected** (after the review): back to the checkpoint's place with full health, mana and ammo; nothing owned is rolled back.
101	- **Modifier keys by weapon type** (`Weapon.Gun.*`), added after the review found the gun enchant also buffed the staff.
102	- **Routing of work between models** (owner's rule): parallel work to Claude subagents, one-batch-at-a-time work to Muse Spark, reviews to Codex.
103	- **Exceptions to "the implementer is Muse Spark"**, with the reason: the project scaffold, the header contracts and the build / test / smoke scripts were written by the architect directly (they are the architecture and its verification); two one-line fixes and the sprite palette script were also direct (smaller than the prompt that would describe them).
104	
105	## Assets created
106	| Asset | Tool (AI or manual) | Prompt or source | License | Machine |
107	|---|---|---|---|---|
108	| 36 placeholder pixel sprites (`Content/Data/Sprites.json`, rows of text) | AI (Claude Opus 5.5 subagent "UI") | Architect's task brief in the session log | Own work | CENTRAL |
109	
110	No third-party assets. Engine content used: the basic shapes and engine materials that ship with UE 5.9.
111	
112	## Problems and solutions
113	- **Trimming plugins did not speed up a warm Editor boot.** We expected a gain; measured, there is none worth the name. Mounted plugins went from 315 to 160, warm boot stayed around 10-11 s. The cost of a warm boot is not in the plugin count. We keep the trimmed list (fewer modules to load and cook) and spent no more time on it.
114	- **Screenshots arrive late.** The engine captures a screenshot a few frames after the request, so in the first smoke run a shot of "the future" showed the inventory that opened right after. The script now leaves a full second after each shot.
115	- Everything else is in "Where the AI failed" above.
116	
117	## Screenshots / clips
118	All taken by the scripted run (`gb.Smoke`) of the second packaged build, not by a person playing.
119	- `media/2026-11-12/1_past_staff.png`: the past. Staff in hand, 90s RPG HUD, an ice wall just cast: a 3D block with a pixel tile, like the stone walls and floor of the arena.
120	- `media/2026-11-12/2_past_gun.png`: pixel-art hands holding the 3D pistol, cyberpunk HUD, the gun enchanted with fire, and a floating damage number.
121	- `media/2026-11-12/9_shield.png`: the summoned ice shield, raised with the Block key.
122	- `media/2026-11-12/3_future_gun.png`: the same place in the future (dark, neon).
123	- `media/2026-11-12/4_inventory.png`, `5_skills.png`: inventory and both skill trees, each tree in its own style.
124	- `media/2026-11-12/6_qte.png`: the spell QTE: key sequence, time bar, power and reach.
125	- `media/2026-11-12/7_death.png`, `8_respawn.png`: death screen and the respawn at the portal, keeping the learned spells.
126	
127	## Numbers of the day
128	- Editor boot, `Total Editor Startup Time` from the log (same machine, same code, empty startup map):
129	
130	| Plugin set | Mounted plugins | Cold (first boot) | Warm boots |
131	|---|---|---|---|
132	| Default + `AllToolsets` (baseline) | 315 | 37.9 s | 10.97 s, 10.96 s |
133	| Trimmed (18 toolsets, 103 defaults off; later 102, see above) | 160 | 16.3 s (first boot after the change) | 10.09 s, 11.15 s |
134	
135	- Code: 103 files, about 17,500 lines; 11 JSON data files.
136	- First full compile of all the parallel work: 3 errors.
137	- Tests: 26 pure-logic tests (24 after the second block), 0.43 s of test time, 15-25 s wall time with the Editor boot.
138	- Smoke run: 31 steps, 40-48 s wall time.
139	- Second block (play-test notes): 56 files changed, 4,428 lines added, 0 compile errors on the first build, 4 review findings; from the owner's message to the second packaged build in one working session.
140	- Build times: first build of the empty module 55 s; incremental builds 2-26 s.
141	- Package: `TeamTBD_Glyphbound.zip`, **245.4 MB** after the second block (245.3 MB the first time; the jam asks for under 1 GB), built in 51-56 s. The packaged exe passes the same scripted run, reading the JSON data as loose files next to it, with the generated material and the runtime navmesh working.
142	- Agent sessions / prompts / external agent runs / MCP calls / commits: see `2026-11-12_DRAFT.md`.
143	
144	## Tools used so far (for the submission's "Tools you used" field)
145	Unreal Engine 5.9.0, Claude Code (Claude Fable 5.2, Claude Opus 5.5), OpenCode (Muse Spark 1.3 Contributor), Codex CLI (GPT Sol 6.1), Unreal Editor MCP server (boot measurements only), git.
146	
147	## Plan for tomorrow
148	- A person plays the second packaged build first, and their notes decide the order of everything else. To check by hand: mouse in menus, the Block key, equipping a second staff from the inventory, enemies around cover, falling off the map, damage numbers.
149	- Tune by playing: movement feel, mouse gesture sensitivity in the QTE, gun viewmodel size, spell numbers.
150	- GDD day 2: gamepad pass, enemy behavior and one real wave, consumables in play, QTE second version, DLSS plugin check for the NVIDIA award.
